commentary_title: LR1 utilisation and tonne-mile demand strengthen amid tighter vessel availability
commentary_summary: LR1 utilisation increased to 93.2% in Week 43, up 2.8 percentage points MoM and 1.2 percentage points YoY, reflecting stronger fleet employment. Demand remained robust, with the tonne-mile index rising to 109.0, up 15.9% YoY, supported by sustained long-haul clean petroleum product movements and firmer trading activity across key routes. | Vessel availability tightened despite a mixed regional picture. Anchored capacity increased by 11.5% MoM in the West and 1.9% MoM in the East, while laden anchor days rose 1.8% on a four-week moving-average basis. The share of laden vessels declined by 10.7 percentage points MoM in the East but increased by 3.9 percentage points in the West, suggesting stronger cargo concentration in Atlantic markets and a more balanced vessel supply-demand position overall. | Market conditions remained supportive as stronger demand outweighed gains in fleet productivity. East ballast speeds increased 10.7% MoM while West ballast speeds fell 13.9% MoM, indicating tighter vessel availability in western markets despite higher bunker prices of $933/tonne.
